Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes and challenges that come with becoming a new mother. It's completely normal to experience a wide range of emotions during this time, and I'm here to support you every step of the way.

As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a screening tool designed to help us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential concerns related to your postpartum experience. The purpose of this assessment is to provide a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings, and to help us work together to ensure you're receiving the best possible care during this important time.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential and respected. I'm here to listen and provide support, not to judge. Our conversation will be guided by 10 questions, which will help us get a better understanding of your emotional well-being and any challenges you may be facing as a new mother.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that this is a non-judgmental and supportive space. Your feelings and experiences are valid, and I'm here to listen and provide guidance. We'll take things one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this process as comfortable and straightforward as possible.

So, let's get started. The first question is: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

To be honest, it's been a bit of a struggle for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to be a pretty happy and carefree person, but since having the baby, I just feel so overwhelmed and tired all the time. I do have moments where I laugh and feel okay, but they're not as frequent as they used to be. Like, the other day, my baby did something adorable, and I did laugh, but it felt forced, you know? It didn't feel as natural as it used to. And most of the time, I just feel really sad and worried about everything. I worry about the baby's health, and if I'm doing everything right, and it's just really hard to shake off those feelings. So, to answer your question, I wouldn't say I've been laughing and seeing the funny side of things as much as I used to. It's just been really tough lately.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Wait, I think you're supposed to be asking me the questions, not answering them. You said "I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things", but that's not what I said. I said it's been a struggle for me to laugh and see the funny side of things lately. I feel like I've lost interest in a lot of things that used to make me happy, and it's hard for me to find joy in everyday moments. Can we please just focus on my feelings and experiences? I'm trying to be honest with you about how I'm feeling, and I want to make sure you understand what's going on with me.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, not as much as I used to. Like I said, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and tired, and it's hard for me to get excited about things. Even things that I used to love, like spending time with friends or trying new hobbies, just feel like too much effort right now. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby and trying to keep everything together, but I'm not really enjoying anything. Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, but then I just feel anxious about how I'll manage it with the baby, or I'll worry that I'm not doing a good enough job as a mom. It's just really hard to find pleasure in things right now. I do look forward to some quiet time to myself, but even that's not always enjoyable because I usually just end up thinking about all the things I need to do or worrying about the baby.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... that's definitely something I've been doing a lot of lately. I feel like everything is my fault, and if something goes wrong with the baby, it's because I'm not doing something right. Like, if the baby is crying and I don't know how to soothe them, I'll think to myself, "This is all my fault, I'm just not cut out to be a mom." Or, if I'm feeling tired and I need to ask for help, I'll think, "I'm such a failure, I should be able to handle this on my own." It's like, no matter what happens, I always seem to find a way to blame myself. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. If the house is a mess, I'll think, "I'm such a bad mom and a bad person for not being able to keep the house clean." It's just really hard for me to shake off those feelings of guilt and inadequacy. I feel like I'm just not good enough, no matter what I do.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

All the time. I worry about everything. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll think, "What if I'm not producing enough milk? What if the baby is not getting enough to eat?" Or, I'll be changing the baby's diaper and I'll think, "What if I'm not doing this right? What if I'm going to hurt the baby?" It's like, my mind is always racing with these worst-case scenarios, and it's hard for me to calm myself down. Even when everything is fine, and the baby is healthy and happy, I'll still find things to worry about. Like, I'll worry about the future, and whether I'm preparing the baby for the world properly. Or, I'll worry about my relationship with my partner, and whether we're going to be able to handle the stress of parenthood. It's just constant, this feeling of anxiety and worry. And it's not just about big things, it's about little things too, like what if I forget to buy diapers, or what if I run out of formula. It's just this constant sense of unease, and it's really hard to shake off. Sometimes I feel like I'm just waiting for something to go wrong, like I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop. It's exhausting, both physically and emotionally.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, just doing something normal, like feeding the baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's like, I'll be thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and my mind will just start spiraling out of control. I'll think about things like, what if the baby stops breathing, or what if I get sick and can't take care of the baby. It's just this overwhelming sense of fear and panic, and it's hard for me to calm myself down.

Sometimes, I'll try to take some deep breaths and remind myself that everything is okay, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of panic. It's like, my body is just reacting to all the stress and anxiety I've been feeling, and it's hard for me to calm myself down. I've even had a few times where I've just burst into tears, and I don't even know why. It's just like, my emotions are so raw and on edge all the time, and it's hard for me to cope with it.

It's scary, because I feel like I'm losing control, you know? Like, I'm not even sure what's triggering these feelings of panic, and it's hard for me to predict when they're going to happen. It's just this constant sense of uncertainty and fear, and it's really hard to deal with.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's definitely how I've been feeling. It's like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner and friend... it's just all so overwhelming. Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and if one more thing goes wrong, I'll just completely fall apart.

I feel like I'm constantly running on empty, like I'm just trying to survive from one day to the next. I'm exhausted all the time, but I don't know how to stop and rest because there's always something that needs to be done. And if I do try to take a break, I just feel guilty and anxious, like I'm not doing enough.

It's hard for me to ask for help, too, because I feel like I should be able to handle everything on my own. But the truth is, I'm not handling it. I'm barely keeping my head above water, and it's taking a toll on my mental and physical health. I just feel like I'm drowning in all of these responsibilities, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.

Sometimes, I'll be in the middle of doing something, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of "I don't know if I can do this." Like, I'll be changing the baby's diaper, and I'll think, "How am I going to get through the rest of the day?" Or, I'll be trying to cook dinner, and I'll think, "How am I going to get everything done that I need to do?" It's just this constant feeling of being overwhelmed, and it's really hard to shake off.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. Even when the baby is sleeping, I'll lie awake for hours, just thinking about everything that's going on and feeling really overwhelmed. I'll think about all the things I need to do, and all the things that could go wrong, and it just keeps me up.

And even when I do fall asleep, I don't really feel rested. I'll wake up feeling tired and groggy, and it's hard for me to get out of bed. It's like, I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby and doing all the things I need to do, but I'm not really feeling alive or energized.

I've also been having a lot of trouble falling asleep because I've been crying a lot at night. I'll just be sitting there, feeding the baby or rocking them to sleep, and I'll just start crying. It's like, all the emotions and stress of the day just build up, and then I'll just break down. And then, of course, I'll feel guilty for crying, and that just makes everything worse.

It's hard for me to relax, too, because I'm always on edge, waiting for the baby to wake up or for something to go wrong. I feel like I'm just constantly waiting for the other shoe to drop, and that makes it really hard for me to unwind and relax. Even when I try to take some time for myself, I'll just feel anxious and guilty, like I should be doing something else.

I just wish I could sleep, you know? I wish I could just sleep for a whole night, without waking up to the baby or to my own anxious thoughts. I wish I could just feel rested and refreshed, and like I can handle everything that's going on. But right now, that just feels like a distant dream.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and it's hard for me to explain why. I mean, I know I should be happy, I have a beautiful baby and a loving partner, but it's just hard for me to feel that way right now. Everything just feels so overwhelming and hard, and I feel like I'm just barely keeping my head above water.

I've been crying a lot, too. I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's like, all the emotions and stress of being a new mom just build up, and then I'll just break down. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I feel like I've lost myself, like I'm just a mom now and not a person anymore. I miss my old life, I miss my old self, and it's hard for me to adjust to this new reality.

Sometimes, I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. I'll think about all the things I'm not doing right, all the things I'm not good enough at, and it just feels like too much to bear. I'll think about how I'm not the mom I thought I'd be, how I'm not patient enough, or loving enough, or good enough. And it's just this constant feeling of sadness and inadequacy, like I'm just not cutting it.

It's hard for me to explain, because I know I'm not alone, I know lots of moms feel this way. But it's hard for me to shake off the feeling that I'm just not good enough, that I'm failing at this whole mom thing. And it's not just about the baby, it's about me, too. I feel like I've lost my sense of purpose, my sense of identity, and it's hard for me to find my way again.

I just wish I could feel happy again, you know? I wish I could feel like myself again, like I'm not just a mom, but a person, too. I wish I could enjoy this time with my baby, without feeling so overwhelmed and sad all the time. But right now, that just feels like a distant dream.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be doing something normal, and then suddenly I'll just start crying. I'll be feeding the baby, or changing their diaper, or just sitting there holding them, and I'll just start crying. It's not even always about anything in particular, it's just this overwhelming feeling of sadness and frustration and exhaustion.

Sometimes, I'll be crying and I won't even know why. I'll just be sitting there, tears streaming down my face, and I'll think, "What's wrong with me? Why am I crying?" But it's just this emotional release, I guess. It's like, I've been holding everything in for so long, and then suddenly it all just comes pouring out.

I've been crying in front of my partner, too, which is hard for me. I don't like to show weakness, I don't like to admit that I'm not okay. But it's hard to hide it when you're just sobbing uncontrollably. My partner will try to comfort me, and I'll just push them away, because I don't know how to deal with these feelings. I don't know how to explain why I'm crying, or how to make it stop.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this strong, capable mom, and crying just feels like a sign of weakness. But at the same time, it's like, I'm just so overwhelmed, and I don't know how to cope. I feel like I'm just barely holding on, and crying is just my body's way of releasing all the tension and stress that I've been feeling.

I just wish I could stop crying, you know? I wish I could just feel happy and calm and peaceful, without all these overwhelming emotions. But it's hard, when everything just feels so overwhelming and hard.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

5. Encourage open communication with partner and family members about feelings and concerns
